## Fix Android crash when scanning QR code

The CHIPTool Android app crashes with an IllegalStateException whenever the user scans a QR code. The root cause is that the BarcodeFragment is not added to the back stack, so when the scan completes and the fragment attempts to navigate back to the host fragment, the reference is null. Ensure all QR scan entry points add the fragment to the back stack so the return navigation works correctly.

61:     val previewRatio = max(width, height).toDouble() / min(width, height)
62:     if (abs(previewRatio - RATIO_4_3_VALUE) <= abs(previewRatio - RATIO_16_9_VALUE)) {
63:       return AspectRatio.RATIO_4_3
64:     }
65:     return AspectRatio.RATIO_16_9
66:   }

68:   override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
69:     super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
70:     if (!hasCameraPermission()) {

73:   }

79:   ): View {
80:     _binding = BarcodeFragmentBinding.inflate(inflater, container, false)

96:   @SuppressLint("UnsafeOptInUsageError")
97:   private fun startCamera() {
98:     val cameraProviderFuture = ProcessCameraProvider.getInstance(requireActivity())
99:     cameraProviderFuture.addListener(
100:       {
101:         val cameraProvider: ProcessCameraProvider = cameraProviderFuture.get()
102:         val metrics = DisplayMetrics().also { binding.cameraView.display?.getRealMetrics(it) }
103:         val screenAspectRatio = aspectRatio(metrics.widthPixels, metrics.heightPixels)
104:         // Preview
105:         val preview: Preview =
106:           Preview.Builder()
107:             .setTargetAspectRatio(screenAspectRatio)
108:             .setTargetRotation(binding.cameraView.display.rotation)
109:             .build()
110:         preview.setSurfaceProvider(binding.cameraView.surfaceProvider)
111: 
112:         // Setup barcode scanner
113:         val imageAnalysis =

115:             .setTargetAspectRatio(screenAspectRatio)
116:             .setTargetRotation(binding.cameraView.display.rotation)
117:             .build()
118:         val cameraExecutor = Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor()
119:         val barcodeScanner: BarcodeScanner = BarcodeScanning.getClient()

125:         try {

127:           cameraProvider.unbindAll()
128: 
129:           // Bind use cases to camera

131:         } catch (exc: Exception) {
132:           Log.e(TAG, "Use case binding failed", exc)
133:         }
134:       },
135:       ContextCompat.getMainExecutor(requireActivity())

147:   private fun processImageProxy(barcodeScanner: BarcodeScanner, imageProxy: ImageProxy) {

153:       .addOnSuccessListener { barcodes -> barcodes.forEach { handleScannedQrCode(it) } }
154:       .addOnFailureListener { Log.e(TAG, it.message ?: it.toString()) }

24: object FragmentUtil {
25:   /**
26:    * Resolves a host of this Fragment as an instance of the specified class. The first of either the
27:    * parent Fragment or the host Activity which implements this interface will be returned.
28:    *
29:    * @param source the Fragment whose host should be retrieved
30:    * @param hostClass the interface which the host must implement
31:    * @throws IllegalStateException if neither host implements <var>hostClass</var>
32:    */
33:   @JvmStatic
34:   fun <T> getHost(source: Fragment, hostClass: Class<T>): T? {
35:     val activity = source.activity
36:     val parentFragment = source.parentFragment
37:     return when {
38:       hostClass.isInstance(parentFragment) -> hostClass.cast(parentFragment)
39:       hostClass.isInstance(activity) -> hostClass.cast(activity)
40:       else -> {
41:         val activityName = activity?.let { it::class.java.simpleName }
42:         val parentName = parentFragment?.let { it::class.java.simpleName }
43:         val exceptionString =
44:           String.format(
45:             Locale.ROOT,
46:             "Neither the parent Fragment $parentName nor the host Activity" +
47:               " $activityName of ${source::class.java.simpleName} implement" +
48:               " ${hostClass.simpleName}."
49:           )
50:         throw IllegalStateException(exceptionString)
51:       }
52:     }
53:   }

We need to extend the ESP32 platform's OTA capabilities to support delta OTA updates. Delta OTA allows more efficient firmware updates by transmitting only the changes between current and new firmware versions rather than the full image.

    The goal is to:
    1. Add a Kconfig option to enable delta OTA functionality
    2. Integrate the ESP-IDF `esp_delta_ota` component as an optional dependency
    3. Modify the OTA image processor to handle delta OTA patch files (including verification and application)
    4. Document how users can generate and use delta OTA images

    Delta OTA should work alongside existing OTA functionality (encrypted OTA, standard OTA) and be controlled via the new configuration option. The implementation should be isolated under `CONFIG_ENABLE_DELTA_OTA` so it doesn't affect existing behavior when disabled.

## Environment Setup
Check these repo files for build and test setup:
    - `config/esp32/components/chip/CMakeLists.txt` — ESP32 component build configuration
    - `config/esp32/components/chip/Kconfig` — ESP32 configuration options
    - `config/esp32/components/chip/idf_component.yml` — ESP-IDF component dependency manifest
    - For general build/test workflows, review `docs/Makefile` and any Python setup files in `scripts/setup/` (e.g., `scripts/setup/requirements.esp32.txt`)

## Implementation Plan
1. Add a new `ENABLE_DELTA_OTA` boolean config option in `config/esp32/components/chip/Kconfig` under the OTA-related options, depending on `ENABLE_OTA_REQUESTOR`, defaulting to `n`.
    2. Add the `espressif/esp_delta_ota` component (version `^1.1.0`) as a dependency in `config/esp32/components/chip/idf_component.yml`, with a rule for `idf_version >= 4.3`.
    3. In `config/esp32/components/chip/CMakeLists.txt`, add a conditional block that appends the `esp_delta_ota` library to `chip_libraries` when `CONFIG_ENABLE_DELTA_OTA` is set.
    4. Modify `src/platform/ESP32/OTAImageProcessorImpl.h`:
       - Add conditional includes for `esp_delta_ota.h` and `esp_app_format.h` under `CONFIG_ENABLE_DELTA_OTA`
       - Define `IMG_HEADER_LEN` constant from `esp_image_header_t`
       - Add member variables: `mDeltaOTAUpdateHandle`, `deltaOtaCfg`, `patchHeaderVerified`, `chipIdVerified`
       - Add method declarations: `DeltaOTACleanUp`, `VerifyChipId`, `VerifyPatchHeader`, `VerifyHeaderData`, `DeltaOTAReadCallback`, `DeltaOTAWriteCallback`
    5. Modify `src/platform/ESP32/OTAImageProcessorImpl.cpp`:
       - Add conditional includes and defines (magic number, sizes) under `CONFIG_ENABLE_DELTA_OTA`
       - Implement `VerifyChipId` to check the chip ID matches the firmware's expected chip ID
       - Implement `VerifyPatchHeader` to check magic word and SHA-256 of current firmware
       - Implement `VerifyHeaderData` to accumulate and verify the patch header
       - Implement `DeltaOTAReadCallback` to read from the incoming patch data
       - Implement `DeltaOTAWriteCallback` to write decompressed data to the OTA partition
       - Implement `DeltaOTACleanUp` for cleanup
       - Modify `HandlePrepareDownload`, `HandleProcessBlock`, `HandleFinalize`, `HandleAbort` to branch into delta OTA path when `CONFIG_ENABLE_DELTA_OTA` is enabled
    6. Update `docs/guides/esp32/ota.md` to add sections for Delta OTA and Encrypted Delta OTA, explaining configuration options, image generation (using `detools` and the `esp_delta_ota_patch_gen.py` script), and Matter OTA header appending.

126: void OTAImageProcessorImpl::HandlePrepareDownload(intptr_t context)
127: {
128:     auto * imageProcessor = reinterpret_cast<OTAImageProcessorImpl *>(context);
129:     if (imageProcessor == nullptr)
130:     {
131:         ChipLogError(SoftwareUpdate, "ImageProcessor context is null");
132:         return;
133:     }
134:     else if (imageProcessor->mDownloader == nullptr)
135:     {
136:         ChipLogError(SoftwareUpdate, "mDownloader is null");
137:         return;
138:     }
139:     imageProcessor->mOTAUpdatePartition = esp_ota_get_next_update_partition(NULL);
140:     if (imageProcessor->mOTAUpdatePartition == NULL)
141:     {
142:         ChipLogError(SoftwareUpdate, "OTA partition not found");
143:         return;
144:     }
145:     esp_err_t err =
146:         esp_ota_begin(imageProcessor->mOTAUpdatePartition, OTA_WITH_SEQUENTIAL_WRITES, &(imageProcessor->mOTAUpdateHandle));
147:     if (err != ESP_OK)
148:     {
149:         imageProcessor->mDownloader->OnPreparedForDownload(ESP32Utils::MapError(err));
150:         return;
151:     }
152: 
153: #if CONFIG_ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_OTA
154:     CHIP_ERROR chipError = imageProcessor->DecryptStart();
155:     if (chipError != CHIP_NO_ERROR)
156:     {
157:         ChipLogError(SoftwareUpdate, "Failed to start decryption process, err:%" CHIP_ERROR_FORMAT, chipError.Format());
158:         imageProcessor->mDownloader->OnPreparedForDownload(chipError);
159:         return;
160:     }
161: #endif // CONFIG_ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_OTA
162: 
163:     imageProcessor->mHeaderParser.Init();
164:     imageProcessor->mDownloader->OnPreparedForDownload(CHIP_NO_ERROR);
165:     PostOTAStateChangeEvent(DeviceLayer::kOtaDownloadInProgress);
166: }

168: void OTAImageProcessorImpl::HandleFinalize(intptr_t context)
169: {
170:     DeviceLayer::OtaState otaState = DeviceLayer::kOtaDownloadFailed;
171:     auto * imageProcessor          = reinterpret_cast<OTAImageProcessorImpl *>(context);
172:     VerifyOrReturn(imageProcessor, ChipLogError(SoftwareUpdate, "ImageProcessor context is null"));
173: 
174: #if CONFIG_ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_OTA
175:     if (CHIP_NO_ERROR != imageProcessor->DecryptEnd())
176:     {
177:         ChipLogError(SoftwareUpdate, "Failed to end pre encrypted OTA");
178:         esp_ota_abort(imageProcessor->mOTAUpdateHandle);
179:         imageProcessor->ReleaseBlock();
180:         PostOTAStateChangeEvent(DeviceLayer::kOtaDownloadFailed);
181:         return;
182:     }
183: #endif // CONFIG_ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_OTA
184: 
185:     esp_err_t err = esp_ota_end(imageProcessor->mOTAUpdateHandle);
186:     if (err != ESP_OK)
187:     {
188:         if (err == ESP_ERR_OTA_VALIDATE_FAILED)
189:         {
190:             ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Image validation failed, image is corrupted");
191:         }
192:         else
193:         {
194:             ESP_LOGE(TAG, "esp_ota_end failed (%s)!", esp_err_to_name(err));
195:         }
196:     }
197:     else
198:     {
199:         ChipLogProgress(SoftwareUpdate, "OTA image downloaded to offset 0x%" PRIx32, imageProcessor->mOTAUpdatePartition->address);
200:         otaState = DeviceLayer::kOtaDownloadComplete;
201:     }
202: 
203:     imageProcessor->ReleaseBlock();
204:     PostOTAStateChangeEvent(otaState);
205: }

228: void OTAImageProcessorImpl::HandleProcessBlock(intptr_t context)
229: {
230:     auto * imageProcessor = reinterpret_cast<OTAImageProcessorImpl *>(context);
231:     if (imageProcessor == nullptr)
232:     {
233:         ChipLogError(SoftwareUpdate, "ImageProcessor context is null");
234:         return;
235:     }
236:     else if (imageProcessor->mDownloader == nullptr)
237:     {
238:         ChipLogError(SoftwareUpdate, "mDownloader is null");
239:         return;
240:     }
241: 
242:     ByteSpan block = ByteSpan(imageProcessor->mBlock.data(), imageProcessor->mBlock.size());
243: 
244:     CHIP_ERROR error = imageProcessor->ProcessHeader(block);
245:     if (error != CHIP_NO_ERROR)
246:     {
247:         ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to process OTA image header");
248:         imageProcessor->mDownloader->EndDownload(error);
249:         PostOTAStateChangeEvent(DeviceLayer::kOtaDownloadFailed);
250:         return;
251:     }
252: 
253:     esp_err_t err;
254:     ByteSpan blockToWrite = block;
255: 
256: #if CONFIG_ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_OTA
257:     error = imageProcessor->DecryptBlock(block, blockToWrite);
258:     if (error != CHIP_NO_ERROR)
259:     {
260:         ChipLogError(SoftwareUpdate, "esp_encrypted_img_decrypt_data failed err:%d", err);
261:         imageProcessor->mDownloader->EndDownload(CHIP_ERROR_WRITE_FAILED);
262:         PostOTAStateChangeEvent(DeviceLayer::kOtaDownloadFailed);
263:         return;
264:     }
265: #endif // CONFIG_ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_OTA
266: 
267:     err = esp_ota_write(imageProcessor->mOTAUpdateHandle, blockToWrite.data(), blockToWrite.size());
268: 
269: #if CONFIG_ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_OTA
270:     free((void *) (blockToWrite.data()));
271: #endif // CONFIG_ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_OTA
272: 
273:     if (err != ESP_OK)
274:     {
275:         ESP_LOGE(TAG, "esp_ota_write failed (%s)", esp_err_to_name(err));
276:         imageProcessor->mDownloader->EndDownload(CHIP_ERROR_WRITE_FAILED);
277:         PostOTAStateChangeEvent(DeviceLayer::kOtaDownloadFailed);
278:         return;
279:     }
280: 
281:     imageProcessor->mParams.downloadedBytes += blockToWrite.size();
282:     imageProcessor->mDownloader->FetchNextData();
283: }

308: CHIP_ERROR OTAImageProcessorImpl::SetBlock(ByteSpan & block)
309: {
310:     if (block.empty())
311:     {
312:         ReleaseBlock();
313:         return CHIP_NO_ERROR;
314:     }
315:     if (mBlock.size() < block.size())
316:     {
317:         if (!mBlock.empty())
318:         {
319:             ReleaseBlock();
320:         }
321:         uint8_t * mBlock_ptr = static_cast<uint8_t *>(Platform::MemoryAlloc(block.size()));
322:         if (mBlock_ptr == nullptr)
323:         {
324:             return CHIP_ERROR_NO_MEMORY;
325:         }
326:         mBlock = MutableByteSpan(mBlock_ptr, block.size());
327:     }
328:     CHIP_ERROR err = CopySpanToMutableSpan(block, mBlock);
329:     if (err != CHIP_NO_ERROR)
330:     {
331:         ChipLogError(SoftwareUpdate, "Cannot copy block data: %" CHIP_ERROR_FORMAT, err.Format());
332:         return err;
333:     }
334:     return CHIP_NO_ERROR;
335: }
336: 
337: CHIP_ERROR OTAImageProcessorImpl::ReleaseBlock()
338: {
339:     if (mBlock.data() != nullptr)
340:     {
341:         Platform::MemoryFree(mBlock.data());
342:     }
343:     mBlock = MutableByteSpan();
344:     return CHIP_NO_ERROR;
345: }

347: CHIP_ERROR OTAImageProcessorImpl::ProcessHeader(ByteSpan & block)
348: {
349:     if (mHeaderParser.IsInitialized())
350:     {
351:         OTAImageHeader header;
352:         CHIP_ERROR error = mHeaderParser.AccumulateAndDecode(block, header);
353: 
354:         // Need more data to decode the header
355:         ReturnErrorCodeIf(error == CHIP_ERROR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL, CHIP_NO_ERROR);
356:         ReturnErrorOnFailure(error);
357: 
358:         mParams.totalFileBytes = header.mPayloadSize;
359:         mHeaderParser.Clear();
360:     }
361: 
362:     return CHIP_NO_ERROR;
363: }

415: CHIP_ERROR OTAImageProcessorImpl::DecryptBlock(const ByteSpan & blockToDecrypt, ByteSpan & decryptedBlock)
416: {
417:     VerifyOrReturnError(mEncryptedOTAEnabled, CHIP_ERROR_INCORRECT_STATE);
418:     VerifyOrReturnError(mOTADecryptionHandle, CHIP_ERROR_INCORRECT_STATE);
419: 
420:     pre_enc_decrypt_arg_t preEncOtaDecryptArgs = {
421:         .data_in      = reinterpret_cast<const char *>(blockToDecrypt.data()),
422:         .data_in_len  = blockToDecrypt.size(),
423:         .data_out     = nullptr,
424:         .data_out_len = 0,
425:     };
426: 
427:     esp_err_t err = esp_encrypted_img_decrypt_data(mOTADecryptionHandle, &preEncOtaDecryptArgs);
428:     if (err != ESP_OK && err != ESP_ERR_NOT_FINISHED)
429:     {
430:         ChipLogError(SoftwareUpdate, "esp_encrypted_img_decrypt_data failed err:%d", err);
431:         return ESP32Utils::MapError(err);
432:     }
433: 
434:     ChipLogDetail(SoftwareUpdate, "esp_encrypted_img_decrypt_data data_in_len:%u, data_out_len:%u",
435:                   preEncOtaDecryptArgs.data_in_len, preEncOtaDecryptArgs.data_out_len);
436: 
437:     if (preEncOtaDecryptArgs.data_out == nullptr || preEncOtaDecryptArgs.data_out_len <= 0)
438:     {
439:         ChipLogProgress(SoftwareUpdate, "Decrypted data is null or out len is zero");
440:     }
441: 
442:     decryptedBlock = ByteSpan(reinterpret_cast<const uint8_t *>(preEncOtaDecryptArgs.data_out), preEncOtaDecryptArgs.data_out_len);
443:     return CHIP_NO_ERROR;
444: }

1: # Matter OTA
2: 
3: ## Generate CHIP OTA image
4: 
5: User can generate the Matter OTA image by simply enabling
6: `CONFIG_CHIP_OTA_IMAGE_BUILD` config option. OTA image is generated in `build`
7: directory with name `<project name>-ota.bin`. This image then can be used with
8: OTA Provider Application.
9: 
10: Please make sure that version number is set to correct value. Use
11: `CONFIG_DEVICE_SOFTWARE_VERSION` and `CONFIG_DEVICE_SOFTWARE_VERSION_NUMBER`
12: config options for setting software version.
13: 
14: Matter OTA image can also be generated using
15: [ota_image_tool.py](https://github.com/project-chip/connectedhomeip/blob/master/src/app/ota_image_tool.py)
16: script.
17: 
18: ## Enabling OTA Requestor
19: 
20: -   Please make sure `CONFIG_ENABLE_OTA_REQUESTOR` config option is enabled for
21:     enabling OTA requestor feature.
22: -   Currently all-clusters-app, lighting-app, and ota-requestor-app supports OTA
23:     requestor functionality.
24: -   Build and flash any supported app, and commission it.
25: 
26: ## Setup OTA Provider app
27: 
28: Setup any of the OTA Provider, commission it and install the appropriate access
29: control list.
30: 
31: -   [Linux OTA Provider](../../../examples/ota-provider-app/linux)
32: -   [ESP32 OTA Provider](../../../examples/ota-provider-app/esp32)
33: 
34: ## Query for an OTA Image
35: 
36: ### Using Console
37: 
38: After commissioning is successful, read the default-otaproviders list of
39: requestor using the command below.
40: 
41: ```
42: ./out/debug/chip-tool otasoftwareupdaterequestor read default-otaproviders <REQUESTOR NODE ID> 0
43: ```
44: 
45: If the list does not have your provider, write into default-otaproviders list of
46: requestor using the command below.
47: 
48: ```
49: ./out/debug/chip-tool otasoftwareupdaterequestor write default-otaproviders '[{"fabricIndex": 1, "providerNodeID": <PROVIDER_NODE_ID_1>, "endpoint": 0}, {"fabricIndex": 1, "providerNodeID": <PROVIDER_NODE_ID_2>, "endpoint": 0}]' <REQUESTOR_NODE_ID> 0
50: ```
51: 
52: Press Enter in requestor device console and type below query.
53: 
54: ```
55: >matter ota query
56: ```
57: 
58: Once the transfer is complete, OTA requestor sends ApplyUpdateRequest command to
59: OTA provider for applying the image. Device will restart on successful
60: application of OTA image.
61: 
62: ### Using chip-tool
63: 
64: After commissioning is successful, announce OTA provider's presence using
65: chip-tool. On receiving this command OTA requestor will query for OTA image.
66: 
67: ```
68: ./out/debug/chip-tool otasoftwareupdaterequestor announce-otaprovider <PROVIDER NODE ID> 0 0 0 <REQUESTOR NODE ID> 0
69: ```
70: 
71: ## Encrypted OTA
72: 
73: ESP32 supports transferring encrypted OTA images. Currently, an application
74: image can be encrypted/decrypted using an RSA-3072 key pair.
75: 
76: ### Firmware Changes
77: 
78: -   Enable configuration options for OTA requestor and Encrypted OTA:
79: 
80:     ```
81:     CONFIG_ENABLE_OTA_REQUESTOR=y
82:     CONFIG_ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_OTA=y
83:     ```
84: 
85: -   Applications need to provide the key pair to the OTA image processor using
86:     the `InitEncryptedOTA()` API to decrypt the received OTA image.
87: 
88: -   For testing purposes, in `examples/lighting-app/esp32`, there is a logic of
89:     embedding the private key in the firmware. To quickly test, please generate
90:     the key pair and rename it as `esp_image_encryption_public_key.pem` and copy
91:     it to directory `examples/lighting-app/esp32`.
92: 
93: Please follow the steps below to generate an application image for OTA upgrades:
94: 
95: 1. Generate a new RSA-3072 key pair or use an existing one.
96: 
97:     - To generate a key pair, use the following command:
98: 
99:         ```
100:         openssl genrsa -out esp_image_encryption_key.pem 3072
101:         ```
102: 
103:     - Extract the public key from the key pair:
104:         ```
105:         openssl rsa -in esp_image_encryption_key.pem -pubout -out esp_image_encryption_public_key.pem
106:         ```
107: 
108: 2. Encrypt the application binary using the
109:    [esp_enc_img_gen.py](https://github.com/espressif/idf-extra-components/blob/master/esp_encrypted_img/tools/esp_enc_img_gen.py)
110:    script.
111: 
112:     - Use the following command to encrypt the OTA image with the public key:
113: 
114:         ```
115:         python3 esp_enc_img_gen.py encrypt lighting-app.bin esp_image_encryption_public_key.pem lighting-app-encrypted.bin
116:         ```
117: 
118:     - Append the Matter OTA header:
119:         ```
120:         src/app/ota_image_tool.py create --vendor-id 0xFFF1 --product-id 0x8000 --version 2 --version-str "v2.0" -da sha256 lighting-app-encrypted.bin lighting-app-encrypted-ota.bin
121:         ```
122: 
123: 3. Use the `lighting-app-encrypted-ota.bin` file with the OTA Provider app.

152: void OTAImageProcessorImpl::HandlePrepareDownload(intptr_t context)
153: {
154:     auto * imageProcessor = reinterpret_cast<OTAImageProcessorImpl *>(context);
155:     if (imageProcessor == nullptr)
156:     {
157:         ChipLogError(SoftwareUpdate, "ImageProcessor context is null");
158:         return;
159:     }
160:     else if (imageProcessor->mDownloader == nullptr)
161:     {
162:         ChipLogError(SoftwareUpdate, "mDownloader is null");
163:         return;
164:     }
165:     imageProcessor->mOTAUpdatePartition = esp_ota_get_next_update_partition(NULL);
166:     if (imageProcessor->mOTAUpdatePartition == NULL)
167:     {
168:         ChipLogError(SoftwareUpdate, "OTA partition not found");
169:         return;
170:     }
171:     esp_err_t err =
172:         esp_ota_begin(imageProcessor->mOTAUpdatePartition, OTA_WITH_SEQUENTIAL_WRITES, &(imageProcessor->mOTAUpdateHandle));
173:     if (err != ESP_OK)
174:     {
175:         imageProcessor->mDownloader->OnPreparedForDownload(ESP32Utils::MapError(err));
176:         return;
177:     }
178: 
179: #if CONFIG_ENABLE_DELTA_OTA
180:     esp_delta_ota_cfg_t * deltaOtaCfg = &(imageProcessor->deltaOtaCfg);
181:     memset(deltaOtaCfg, 0, sizeof(*deltaOtaCfg));
182: 
183:     deltaOtaCfg->partitions[0]             = esp_ota_get_running_partition();
184:     deltaOtaCfg->partitions[1]             = imageProcessor->mOTAUpdatePartition;
185:     deltaOtaCfg->partitions_num            = 2;
186:     deltaOtaCfg->ota_image_size_limit_size = 0;
187:     deltaOtaCfg->magic_number              = PATCH_HEADER_MAGIC;
188: 
189:     esp_chip_info_t chipInfo;
190:     esp_chip_info(&chipInfo);
191:     deltaOtaCfg->chip_id = static_cast<uint16_t>(chipInfo.model);
192: 
193:     err = esp_partition_get_sha256(deltaOtaCfg->partitions[0], deltaOtaCfg->sha_digest);
194:     if (err != ESP_OK)
195:     {
196:         ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to get running firmware SHA256 digest, esp_err:%d", err);
197:         imageProcessor->mDownloader->OnPreparedForDownload(ESP32Utils::MapError(err));
198:         return;
199:     }
200:     deltaOtaCfg->sha_image_type = ESP_APP_DESC_MAGIC_WORD;
201:     deltaOtaCfg->read           = &OTAImageProcessorImpl::DeltaOTAReadCallback;
202:     deltaOtaCfg->write          = &OTAImageProcessorImpl::DeltaOTAWriteCallback;
203: 
204:     sDeltaOTABasePartition  = deltaOtaCfg->partitions[0];
205:     sDeltaOTABaseReadOffset = 0;
206:     sDeltaOTAWriteHandle    = imageProcessor->mOTAUpdateHandle;
207: 
208:     imageProcessor->mDeltaOTAUpdateHandle = esp_delta_ota_init(deltaOtaCfg);
209:     if (imageProcessor->mDeltaOTAUpdateHandle == nullptr)
210:     {
211:         ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Delta OTA initialization failed");
212:         esp_ota_abort(imageProcessor->mOTAUpdateHandle);
213:         imageProcessor->mDownloader->OnPreparedForDownload(CHIP_ERROR_WRITE_FAILED);
214:         return;
215:     }
216: 
217:     imageProcessor->patchHeaderVerified = false;
218:     imageProcessor->chipIdVerified      = false;
219:     imageProcessor->patchSizeReceived   = 0;
220:     imageProcessor->bytesReceived       = 0;
221: #endif // CONFIG_ENABLE_DELTA_OTA
222: 
223: #if CONFIG_ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_OTA
224:     CHIP_ERROR chipError = imageProcessor->DecryptStart();
225:     if (chipError != CHIP_NO_ERROR)
226:     {
227:         ChipLogError(SoftwareUpdate, "Failed to start decryption process, err:%" CHIP_ERROR_FORMAT, chipError.Format());
228:         imageProcessor->mDownloader->OnPreparedForDownload(chipError);
229:         return;
230:     }
231: #endif // CONFIG_ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_OTA
232: 
233:     imageProcessor->mHeaderParser.Init();
234:     imageProcessor->mDownloader->OnPreparedForDownload(CHIP_NO_ERROR);
235:     PostOTAStateChangeEvent(DeviceLayer::kOtaDownloadInProgress);
236: }

238: void OTAImageProcessorImpl::HandleFinalize(intptr_t context)
239: {
240:     DeviceLayer::OtaState otaState = DeviceLayer::kOtaDownloadFailed;
241:     auto * imageProcessor          = reinterpret_cast<OTAImageProcessorImpl *>(context);
242:     VerifyOrReturn(imageProcessor, ChipLogError(SoftwareUpdate, "ImageProcessor context is null"));
243: 
244: #if CONFIG_ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_OTA
245:     if (CHIP_NO_ERROR != imageProcessor->DecryptEnd())
246:     {
247:         ChipLogError(SoftwareUpdate, "Failed to end pre encrypted OTA");
248:         esp_ota_abort(imageProcessor->mOTAUpdateHandle);
249:         imageProcessor->ReleaseBlock();
250:         PostOTAStateChangeEvent(DeviceLayer::kOtaDownloadFailed);
251:         return;
252:     }
253: #endif // CONFIG_ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_OTA
254: 
255: #if CONFIG_ENABLE_DELTA_OTA
256:     BC26Result result = esp_delta_ota_finish(imageProcessor->mDeltaOTAUpdateHandle);
257:     if (result != BC26OK)
258:     {
259:         ESP_LOGE(TAG, "esp_delta_ota_finish failed with %d", result);
260:         imageProcessor->DeltaOTACleanUp();
261:         esp_ota_abort(imageProcessor->mOTAUpdateHandle);
262:         imageProcessor->ReleaseBlock();
263:         PostOTAStateChangeEvent(DeviceLayer::kOtaDownloadFailed);
264:         return;
265:     }
266: #endif // CONFIG_ENABLE_DELTA_OTA
267: 
268:     esp_err_t err = esp_ota_end(imageProcessor->mOTAUpdateHandle);
269:     if (err != ESP_OK)
270:     {
271:         if (err == ESP_ERR_OTA_VALIDATE_FAILED)
272:         {
273:             ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Image validation failed, image is corrupted");
274:         }
275:         else
276:         {
277:             ESP_LOGE(TAG, "esp_ota_end failed (%s)!", esp_err_to_name(err));
278:         }
279:     }
280:     else
281:     {
282:         ChipLogProgress(SoftwareUpdate, "OTA image downloaded to offset 0x%" PRIx32, imageProcessor->mOTAUpdatePartition->address);
283:         otaState = DeviceLayer::kOtaDownloadComplete;
284:     }
285: 
286:     imageProcessor->ReleaseBlock();
287:     PostOTAStateChangeEvent(otaState);
288: }

315: void OTAImageProcessorImpl::HandleProcessBlock(intptr_t context)
316: {
317:     auto * imageProcessor = reinterpret_cast<OTAImageProcessorImpl *>(context);
318:     if (imageProcessor == nullptr)
319:     {
320:         ChipLogError(SoftwareUpdate, "ImageProcessor context is null");
321:         return;
322:     }
323:     else if (imageProcessor->mDownloader == nullptr)
324:     {
325:         ChipLogError(SoftwareUpdate, "mDownloader is null");
326:         return;
327:     }
328: 
329:     ByteSpan block = ByteSpan(imageProcessor->mBlock.data(), imageProcessor->mBlock.size());
330: 
331:     CHIP_ERROR error = imageProcessor->ProcessHeader(block);
332:     if (error != CHIP_NO_ERROR)
333:     {
334:         ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to process OTA image header");
335:         imageProcessor->mDownloader->EndDownload(error);
336:         PostOTAStateChangeEvent(DeviceLayer::kOtaDownloadFailed);
337:         return;
338:     }
339: 
340:     esp_err_t err;
341:     ByteSpan blockToWrite = block;
342: 
343: #if CONFIG_ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_OTA
344:     error = imageProcessor->DecryptBlock(block, blockToWrite);
345:     if (error != CHIP_NO_ERROR)
346:     {
347:         ChipLogError(SoftwareUpdate, "esp_encrypted_img_decrypt_data failed err:%" CHIP_ERROR_FORMAT, error.Format());
348:         imageProcessor->mDownloader->EndDownload(CHIP_ERROR_WRITE_FAILED);
349:         PostOTAStateChangeEvent(DeviceLayer::kOtaDownloadFailed);
350:         return;
351:     }
352: #endif // CONFIG_ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_OTA
353: 
354: #if CONFIG_ENABLE_DELTA_OTA
355:     if (!imageProcessor->patchHeaderVerified)
356:     {
357:         error = imageProcessor->VerifyHeaderData(blockToWrite);
358:         if (error != CHIP_NO_ERROR)
359:         {
360:             ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to process delta OTA patch header");
361: #if CONFIG_ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_OTA
362:             free((void *) (blockToWrite.data()));
363: #endif // CONFIG_ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_OTA
364:             imageProcessor->mDownloader->EndDownload(error);
365:             PostOTAStateChangeEvent(DeviceLayer::kOtaDownloadFailed);
366:             return;
367:         }
368:     }
369: 
370:     // Bytes of the current block that belong to the (already verified) patch
371:     // header must not be forwarded to the delta OTA library.
372:     uint16_t headerBytesInBlock = (imageProcessor->patchHeaderVerified && (imageProcessor->bytesReceived < PATCH_HEADER_LENGTH))
373:         ? static_cast<uint16_t>(PATCH_HEADER_LENGTH - imageProcessor->bytesReceived)
374:         : 0;
375:     imageProcessor->bytesReceived += static_cast<uint16_t>(blockToWrite.size());
376: 
377:     if (imageProcessor->patchHeaderVerified)
378:     {
379:         ByteSpan deltaBlock(blockToWrite.data() + headerBytesInBlock, blockToWrite.size() - headerBytesInBlock);
380:         if (!deltaBlock.empty())
381:         {
382:             BC26Result result = esp_delta_ota_feed_patch(imageProcessor->mDeltaOTAUpdateHandle,
383:                                                          const_cast<uint8_t *>(deltaBlock.data()), deltaBlock.size());
384:             if (result != BC26OK)
385:             {
386:                 ESP_LOGE(TAG, "esp_delta_ota_feed_patch failed with %d", result);
387: #if CONFIG_ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_OTA
388:                 free((void *) (blockToWrite.data()));
389: #endif // CONFIG_ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_OTA
390:                 imageProcessor->mDownloader->EndDownload(CHIP_ERROR_WRITE_FAILED);
391:                 PostOTAStateChangeEvent(DeviceLayer::kOtaDownloadFailed);
392:                 return;
393:             }
394:         }
395:     }
396: 
397: #if CONFIG_ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_OTA
398:     free((void *) (blockToWrite.data()));
399: #endif // CONFIG_ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_OTA
400: 
401:     imageProcessor->mParams.downloadedBytes += blockToWrite.size();
402:     imageProcessor->mDownloader->FetchNextData();
403:     return;
404: #else
405:     err = esp_ota_write(imageProcessor->mOTAUpdateHandle, blockToWrite.data(), blockToWrite.size());
406: 
407: #if CONFIG_ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_OTA
408:     free((void *) (blockToWrite.data()));
409: #endif // CONFIG_ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_OTA
410: 
411:     if (err != ESP_OK)
412:     {
413:         ESP_LOGE(TAG, "esp_ota_write failed (%s)", esp_err_to_name(err));
414:         imageProcessor->mDownloader->EndDownload(CHIP_ERROR_WRITE_FAILED);
415:         PostOTAStateChangeEvent(DeviceLayer::kOtaDownloadFailed);
416:         return;
417:     }
418: 
419:     imageProcessor->mParams.downloadedBytes += blockToWrite.size();
420:     imageProcessor->mDownloader->FetchNextData();
421: #endif // CONFIG_ENABLE_DELTA_OTA
422: }

463: CHIP_ERROR OTAImageProcessorImpl::VerifyChipId(ByteSpan & block)
464: {
465:     // Verify that the delta OTA patch is destined for the chip on which this
466:     // firmware is running. Patch header layout:
467:     // | magic(1) | reserved(3) | patch_size(2) | chip_id(2) | sha256(32) |
468:     if (block.size() < (CHIP_ID_POSITION + CHIP_ID_TYPE_SIZE))
469:     {
470:         return CHIP_ERROR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL;
471:     }
472: 
473:     if (block.data()[0] != PATCH_HEADER_MAGIC)
474:     {
475:         ChipLogError(SoftwareUpdate, "Delta OTA patch header magic mismatch");
476:         return CHIP_ERROR_INVALID_FILE_IDENTIFIER;
477:     }
478: 
479:     uint16_t chipId = 0;
480:     memcpy(&chipId, block.data() + CHIP_ID_POSITION, CHIP_ID_TYPE_SIZE);
481: 
482:     esp_chip_info_t chipInfo;
483:     esp_chip_info(&chipInfo);
484:     if (static_cast<uint16_t>(chipInfo.model) != chipId)
485:     {
486:         ChipLogError(SoftwareUpdate, "Delta OTA patch chip id mismatch, expected %u, got %u", chipId,
487:                      static_cast<uint16_t>(chipInfo.model));
488:         return CHIP_ERROR_INVALID_FILE_IDENTIFIER;
489:     }
490: 
491:     chipIdVerified = true;
492:     return CHIP_NO_ERROR;
493: }
494: 
495: CHIP_ERROR OTAImageProcessorImpl::VerifyPatchHeader(ByteSpan & block)
496: {
497:     if (block.size() < PATCH_HEADER_LENGTH)
498:     {
499:         return CHIP_ERROR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL;
500:     }
501: 
502:     if (block.data()[0] != PATCH_HEADER_MAGIC)
503:     {
504:         ChipLogError(SoftwareUpdate, "Delta OTA patch header magic mismatch");
505:         return CHIP_ERROR_INVALID_FILE_IDENTIFIER;
506:     }
507: 
508:     uint16_t patchSize = 0;
509:     memcpy(&patchSize, block.data() + PATCH_SIZE_POSITION, PATCH_SIZE_TYPE_SIZE);
510:     if (patchSize == 0 || patchSize > PATCH_SIZE_MASK)
511:     {
512:         ChipLogError(SoftwareUpdate, "Invalid delta OTA patch size %u", patchSize);
513:         return CHIP_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
514:     }
515: 
516:     // The SHA256 digest recorded in the patch header must match the digest of
517:     // the currently running firmware, since the patch is created against it.
518:     uint8_t expectedSha[SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH] = { 0 };
519:     memcpy(expectedSha, block.data() + SHA256_DIGEST_POSITION, SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH);
520: 
521:     uint8_t runningSha[SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH] = { 0 };
522:     esp_err_t err                            = esp_partition_get_sha256(esp_ota_get_running_partition(), runningSha);
523:     if (err != ESP_OK)
524:     {
525:         ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to get running firmware SHA256 digest, esp_err:%d", err);
526:         return ESP32Utils::MapError(err);
527:     }
528: 
529:     if (memcmp(expectedSha, runningSha, SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH) != 0)
530:     {
531:         ChipLogError(SoftwareUpdate, "Delta OTA patch SHA256 digest mismatch");
532:         return CHIP_ERROR_INVALID_FILE_IDENTIFIER;
533:     }
534: 
535:     patchHeaderVerified = true;
536:     return CHIP_NO_ERROR;
537: }
538: 
539: CHIP_ERROR OTAImageProcessorImpl::VerifyHeaderData(ByteSpan & block)
540: {
541:     // The delta OTA patch header (PATCH_HEADER_LENGTH bytes) may span multiple
542:     // download blocks, so accumulate it before running any verification on it.
543:     size_t toCopy = block.size();
544:     if (toCopy > static_cast<size_t>(PATCH_HEADER_LENGTH - patchSizeReceived))
545:     {
546:         toCopy = static_cast<size_t>(PATCH_HEADER_LENGTH - patchSizeReceived);
547:     }
548: 
549:     if (toCopy > 0)
550:     {
551:         memcpy(headersReceived + patchSizeReceived, block.data(), toCopy);
552:         patchSizeReceived += static_cast<uint16_t>(toCopy);
553:     }
554: 
555:     if (patchSizeReceived < PATCH_HEADER_LENGTH)
556:     {
557:         // The complete patch header has not been received yet.
558:         return CHIP_NO_ERROR;
559:     }
560: 
561:     ByteSpan header(headersReceived, PATCH_HEADER_LENGTH);
562: 
563:     if (!chipIdVerified)
564:     {
565:         ReturnErrorOnFailure(VerifyChipId(header));
566:     }
567:     ReturnErrorOnFailure(VerifyPatchHeader(header));
568: 
569:     return CHIP_NO_ERROR;
570: }

572: BC26Result OTAImageProcessorImpl::DeltaOTAReadCallback(void * handle, size_t * size, void * data)
573: {
574:     (void) handle;
575: 
576:     if (size == nullptr || data == nullptr)
577:     {
578:         return BC_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
579:     }
580: 
581:     if (sDeltaOTABasePartition == nullptr)
582:     {
583:         return BC_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
584:     }
585: 
586:     // Provide the base (currently running) firmware image to the delta OTA
587:     // library in sequential chunks.
588:     if (sDeltaOTABaseReadOffset >= sDeltaOTABasePartition->size)
589:     {
590:         *size = 0;
591:         return BC26OK;
592:     }
593: 
594:     size_t bytesToRead = *size;
595:     if (bytesToRead > (sDeltaOTABasePartition->size - sDeltaOTABaseReadOffset))
596:     {
597:         bytesToRead = sDeltaOTABasePartition->size - sDeltaOTABaseReadOffset;
598:     }
599: 
600:     esp_err_t err = esp_partition_read(sDeltaOTABasePartition, sDeltaOTABaseReadOffset, data, bytesToRead);
601:     if (err != ESP_OK)
602:     {
603:         ESP_LOGE(TAG, "esp_partition_read failed (%s)", esp_err_to_name(err));
604:         return BC_ERR_FLASH_WRITE_FAIL;
605:     }
606: 
607:     sDeltaOTABaseReadOffset += bytesToRead;
608:     *size = bytesToRead;
609:     return BC26OK;
610: }
611: 
612: BC26Result OTAImageProcessorImpl::DeltaOTAWriteCallback(void * handle, size_t size, uint8_t * data)
613: {
614:     (void) handle;
615: 
616:     if (size == 0 || data == nullptr)
617:     {
618:         return BC_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
619:     }
620: 
621:     // Persist the decompressed image produced by the delta OTA library.
622:     esp_err_t err = esp_ota_write(sDeltaOTAWriteHandle, data, size);
623:     if (err != ESP_OK)
624:     {
625:         ESP_LOGE(TAG, "esp_ota_write failed (%s)", esp_err_to_name(err));
626:         return BC_ERR_FLASH_WRITE_FAIL;
627:     }
628: 
629:     return BC26OK;
630: }
631: #endif // CONFIG_ENABLE_DELTA_OTA

633: CHIP_ERROR OTAImageProcessorImpl::SetBlock(ByteSpan & block)
634: {
635:     if (block.empty())
636:     {
637:         ReleaseBlock();
638:         return CHIP_NO_ERROR;
639:     }
640:     if (mBlock.size() < block.size())
641:     {
642:         if (!mBlock.empty())
643:         {
644:             ReleaseBlock();
645:         }
646:         uint8_t * mBlock_ptr = static_cast<uint8_t *>(Platform::MemoryAlloc(block.size()));
647:         if (mBlock_ptr == nullptr)
648:         {
649:             return CHIP_ERROR_NO_MEMORY;
650:         }
651:         mBlock = MutableByteSpan(mBlock_ptr, block.size());
652:     }
653:     CHIP_ERROR err = CopySpanToMutableSpan(block, mBlock);
654:     if (err != CHIP_NO_ERROR)
655:     {
656:         ChipLogError(SoftwareUpdate, "Cannot copy block data: %" CHIP_ERROR_FORMAT, err.Format());
657:         return err;
658:     }
659:     return CHIP_NO_ERROR;
660: }

662: CHIP_ERROR OTAImageProcessorImpl::ReleaseBlock()
663: {

668:     mBlock = MutableByteSpan();
669:     return CHIP_NO_ERROR;

672: CHIP_ERROR OTAImageProcessorImpl::ProcessHeader(ByteSpan & block)
673: {
674:     if (mHeaderParser.IsInitialized())
675:     {
676:         OTAImageHeader header;
677:         CHIP_ERROR error = mHeaderParser.AccumulateAndDecode(block, header);
678: 
679:         // Need more data to decode the header
680:         ReturnErrorCodeIf(error == CHIP_ERROR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL, CHIP_NO_ERROR);
681:         ReturnErrorOnFailure(error);
682: 
683:         mParams.totalFileBytes = header.mPayloadSize;
684:         mHeaderParser.Clear();
685:     }
686: 
687:     return CHIP_NO_ERROR;
688: }

728: void OTAImageProcessorImpl::DecryptAbort()
729: {

arguments.newString:
3. Use the `lighting-app-encrypted-ota.bin` file with the OTA Provider app.

## Delta OTA

ESP32 supports delta OTA updates, which allow transferring only the changes
between the currently running firmware and the new firmware, instead of the
full image. Delta OTA works alongside the standard and encrypted OTA flows and
is controlled by the `CONFIG_ENABLE_DELTA_OTA` configuration option.

### Firmware Changes

-   Enable configuration options for OTA requestor and Delta OTA:

    ```
    CONFIG_ENABLE_OTA_REQUESTOR=y
    CONFIG_ENABLE_DELTA_OTA=y
    ```

    When `CONFIG_ENABLE_DELTA_OTA` is enabled, the
    [esp_delta_ota](https://github.com/espressif/idf-extra-components/tree/master/esp_delta_ota)
    component is pulled in automatically as a dependency.

### Generate Delta OTA image

1.  Install [detools](https://pypi.org/project/detools/) which is used by the
    patch generator to create the delta patch:

    ```
    pip install detools
    ```

2.  Generate a delta patch between the firmware currently running on the device
    (base image) and the new firmware:

    ```
    python3 esp_delta_ota_patch_gen.py <path-to-base-image.bin> <path-to-new-image.bin> <path-to-delta-patch.bin>
    ```

    The `esp_delta_ota_patch_gen.py` script is part of the `esp_delta_ota`
    component and is available in its `tools/` directory.

3.  Append the Matter OTA header:

    ```
    src/app/ota_image_tool.py create --vendor-id 0xFFF1 --product-id 0x8000 --version 2 --version-str "v2.0" -da sha256 <path-to-delta-patch.bin> <path-to-delta-patch-ota.bin>
    ```

4.  Use the `<path-to-delta-patch-ota.bin>` file with the OTA Provider app.

>   **Note:** A delta patch is created against a specific base firmware image.
>   On the device, the chip ID and the SHA-256 digest of the currently running
>   firmware are checked against the values recorded in the patch header before
>   the patch is applied. The base image must therefore match the firmware
>   running on the device.

## Encrypted Delta OTA

A delta OTA patch can also be encrypted, like a regular application image,
using an RSA-3072 key pair.

-   Enable configuration options for OTA requestor, Encrypted OTA and Delta OTA:

    ```
    CONFIG_ENABLE_OTA_REQUESTOR=y
    CONFIG_ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_OTA=y
    CONFIG_ENABLE_DELTA_OTA=y
    ```

-   Applications need to provide the key pair to the OTA image processor using
    the `InitEncryptedOTA()` API to decrypt the received delta patch.

1.  Generate a delta patch as described in the [Delta OTA](#delta-ota) section.

2.  Encrypt the delta patch using the
    [esp_enc_img_gen.py](https://github.com/espressif/idf-extra-components/blob/master/esp_encrypted_img/tools/esp_enc_img_gen.py)
    script:

    ```
    python3 esp_enc_img_gen.py encrypt <path-to-delta-patch.bin> esp_image_encryption_public_key.pem <path-to-delta-patch-encrypted.bin>
    ```

3.  Append the Matter OTA header:

    ```
    src/app/ota_image_tool.py create --vendor-id 0xFFF1 --product-id 0x8000 --version 2 --version-str "v2.0" -da sha256 <path-to-delta-patch-encrypted.bin> <path-to-delta-patch-encrypted-ota.bin>
    ```

4.  Use the `<path-to-delta-patch-encrypted-ota.bin>` file with the OTA Provider
    app.

 3. Use the `lighting-app-encrypted-ota.bin` file with the OTA Provider app.
+
+## Delta OTA
+
+Delta OTA Updates is a feature that enables Over-the-Air (OTA) firmware update
+with compressed delta binaries. Patch files have smaller size than the original
+firmware file, which reduces the time and network usage to download the file
+from the server. Also, no additional storage partition is required for the
+"patch".
+
+### Firmware Changes
+
+-   Enable configuration options for OTA requestor and Delta OTA:
+
+    ```
+    CONFIG_ENABLE_OTA_REQUESTOR=y
+    CONFIG_ENABLE_DELTA_OTA=y
+    ```
+
+Please follow the steps below to generate an application image for OTA upgrades:
+
+1. Delta binary needs to be generated using binary delta encoding in Python
+   3.6+. You can install `detools` using the following command.
+
+    ```
+    pip install detools>=0.49.0
+    ```
+
+2. Generate delta binary.
+
+    ```
+    python managed_components/espressif__esp_delta_ota/examples/https_delta_ota/tools/esp_delta_ota_patch_gen.py --chip <chip> --base_binary <base-binary> --new_binary <new-binary> --patch_file_name <patch-file-name.bin>
+    ```
+
+3. Append the Matter OTA header:
+   `src/app/ota_image_tool.py create --vendor-id 0xFFF1 --product-id 0x8000 --version 2 --version-str "v2.0" -da sha256 <patch-file-name.bin> lighting-app-delta-ota.bin`
+
+4. Use the `lighting-app-delta-ota.bin` file with the OTA Provider app.
+
+## Encrypted Delta OTA
+
+To use encrypted delta OTA, follow the below steps.
+
+### Firmware Changes
+
+-   Enable configuration options for OTA requestor, Delta OTA and Encrypted OTA:
+
+    ```
+    CONFIG_ENABLE_OTA_REQUESTOR=y
+    CONFIG_ENABLE_DELTA_OTA=y
+    CONFIG_ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_OTA=y
+    ```

+1. Follow the step of `Generate a new RSA-3072 key pair or use an existing one`
+   of

+   to build your binary.

+2. Create delta binary as shown in `Generate delta binary` of

+3. Encrypt the application binary.
+

arguments.oldString:
## Delta OTA

ESP32 supports delta OTA updates, which allow transferring only the changes
between the currently running firmware and the new firmware, instead of the
full image. Delta OTA works alongside the standard and encrypted OTA flows and
is controlled by the `CONFIG_ENABLE_DELTA_OTA` configuration option.

### Firmware Changes

-   Enable configuration options for OTA requestor and Delta OTA:

    ```
    CONFIG_ENABLE_OTA_REQUESTOR=y
    CONFIG_ENABLE_DELTA_OTA=y
    ```

    When `CONFIG_ENABLE_DELTA_OTA` is enabled, the
    [esp_delta_ota](https://github.com/espressif/idf-extra-components/tree/master/esp_delta_ota)
    component is pulled in automatically as a dependency.

### Generate Delta OTA image

1.  Install [detools](https://pypi.org/project/detools/) which is used by the
    patch generator to create the delta patch:

    ```
    pip install detools
    ```

2.  Generate a delta patch between the firmware currently running on the device
    (base image) and the new firmware:

    ```
    python3 esp_delta_ota_patch_gen.py <path-to-base-image.bin> <path-to-new-image.bin> <path-to-delta-patch.bin>
    ```

    The `esp_delta_ota_patch_gen.py` script is part of the `esp_delta_ota`
    component and is available in its `tools/` directory.

3.  Append the Matter OTA header:

    ```
    src/app/ota_image_tool.py create --vendor-id 0xFFF1 --product-id 0x8000 --version 2 --version-str "v2.0" -da sha256 <path-to-delta-patch.bin> <path-to-delta-patch-ota.bin>
    ```

4.  Use the `<path-to-delta-patch-ota.bin>` file with the OTA Provider app.

>   **Note:** A delta patch is created against a specific base firmware image.
>   On the device, the chip ID and the SHA-256 digest of the currently running
>   firmware are checked against the values recorded in the patch header before
>   the patch is applied. The base image must therefore match the firmware
>   running on the device.

## Encrypted Delta OTA

A delta OTA patch can also be encrypted, like a regular application image,
using an RSA-3072 key pair.

-   Enable configuration options for OTA requestor, Encrypted OTA and Delta OTA:

    ```
    CONFIG_ENABLE_OTA_REQUESTOR=y
    CONFIG_ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_OTA=y
    CONFIG_ENABLE_DELTA_OTA=y
    ```

-   Applications need to provide the key pair to the OTA image processor using
    the `InitEncryptedOTA()` API to decrypt the received delta patch.

1.  Generate a delta patch as described in the [Delta OTA](#delta-ota) section.

2.  Encrypt the delta patch using the
    [esp_enc_img_gen.py](https://github.com/espressif/idf-extra-components/blob/master/esp_encrypted_img/tools/esp_enc_img_gen.py)
    script:

    ```
    python3 esp_enc_img_gen.py encrypt <path-to-delta-patch.bin> esp_image_encryption_public_key.pem <path-to-delta-patch-encrypted.bin>
    ```

3.  Append the Matter OTA header:

    ```
    src/app/ota_image_tool.py create --vendor-id 0xFFF1 --product-id 0x8000 --version 2 --version-str "v2.0" -da sha256 <path-to-delta-patch-encrypted.bin> <path-to-delta-patch-encrypted-ota.bin>
    ```

4.  Use the `<path-to-delta-patch-encrypted-ota.bin>` file with the OTA Provider
    app.

249:             self.extra_gn_options.append(f"wiseconnect_sdk_root=\"{wiseconnect_sdk_path}\"")

251:         if "WIFI_SDK_ROOT" in os.environ and enable_917_soc:

253:             self.extra_gn_options.append(f"wifi_sdk_root=\"{wifi_sdk_path}\"")

258:     def build_outputs(self):
259:         items = {}
260:         for extension in ["out", "out.map", "hex"]:
261:             name = '%s.%s' % (self.app.AppNamePrefix(), extension)
262:             items[name] = os.path.join(self.output_dir, name)
263: 
264:         if self.app == Efr32App.UNIT_TEST:
265:             # Include test runner python wheels
266:             for root, dirs, files in os.walk(os.path.join(self.output_dir, 'chip_nl_test_runner_wheels')):
267:                 for file in files:
268:                     items["chip_nl_test_runner_wheels/" +
269:                           file] = os.path.join(root, file)
270: 
271:         # Figure out flash bundle files and build accordingly
272:         with open(os.path.join(self.output_dir, self.app.FlashBundleName())) as f:
273:             for line in f.readlines():
274:                 name = line.strip()
275:                 items['flashbundle/%s' %
276:                       name] = os.path.join(self.output_dir, name)
277: 
278:         return items

280:     def generate(self):
281:         cmd = [
282:             'gn', 'gen', '--check', '--fail-on-unused-args',
283:             '--export-compile-commands',
284:             '--root=%s' % self.root
285:         ]
286:         if self.dotfile:
287:             cmd += ['--dotfile=%s' % self.dotfile]
288: 
289:         extra_args = self.GnBuildArgs()
290: 
291:         if self.options.pw_command_launcher:
292:             extra_args.append('pw_command_launcher="%s"' % self.options.pw_command_launcher)
293: 
294:         if self.options.pregen_dir:
295:             extra_args.append('chip_code_pre_generated_directory="%s"' % self.options.pregen_dir)
296: 
297:         if extra_args:
298:             cmd += ['--args=%s' % ' '.join(extra_args)]
299: 
300:         cmd += [self.output_dir]
301: 
302:         title = 'Generating ' + self.identifier
303:         extra_env = self.GnBuildEnv()
304: 
305:         if extra_env:
306:             # convert the command into a bash command that includes
307:             # setting environment variables
308:             cmd = [
309:                 'bash', '-c', '\n' + ' '.join(
310:                     ['%s="%s" \\\n' % (key, value) for key, value in extra_env.items()] +
311:                     [shlex.join(cmd)]
312:                 )
313:             ]
314: 
315:         self._Execute(cmd, title=title)

We need to migrate the Access Control test suite from the legacy `nlunit-test` framework to the Pigweed `pw_unit_test` framework. This is part of a larger project to phase out `nlunit-test` across the codebase.

    The current test file `src/access/tests/TestAccessControl.cpp` uses `nlunit-test` macros like `NL_TEST_ASSERT`, `nlTestSuite`, and `CHIP_REGISTER_TEST_SUITE`. We need to rewrite these tests to use GoogleTest-compatible `pw_unit_test` macros (`EXPECT_EQ`, `EXPECT_NE`, `TEST_F`, etc.) and update the GN build configuration accordingly.

    The goal is to:
    1. Convert `src/access/tests/TestAccessControl.cpp` to use `pw_unit_test` (GoogleTest-style) macros and fixtures.
    2. Change the build target from `chip_test_suite_using_nltest` to the standard `chip_test_suite` template.
    3. Update the `chip_test_suite` GN template to properly support `pw_unit_test` dependencies.
    4. Update the OpenIoT SDK test component lists to reflect the framework migration.

    Please ensure that all test logic is preserved and that the migration does not alter test behavior or coverage.

## Environment Setup
Check `build/chip/chip_test_suite.gni` for the test suite template definitions. The `src/access/tests/BUILD.gn` file controls the build for this specific test target. Also review `build_overrides/pigweed.gni` and `build_overrides/nlunit_test.gni` for framework paths. The `src/test_driver/openiotsdk/unit-tests/CMakeLists.txt` and the `test_components*.txt` files describe the OpenIoT SDK test setup. For general project testing guidance, look at `docs/` for testing documentation.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Modify `build/chip/chip_test_suite.gni`**:
       - Remove the `nlunit-test` dependency references from the template's documentation comments.
       - Add `deps = [ dir_pw_unit_test ]` to the `chip_test_suite` template so all suites automatically depend on `pw_unit_test`.
       - Add an `output_dir` variable to the `pw_test` targets created in the template, defaulting to `"${root_out_dir}/tests"` and honor an optional `output_dir` from the invoker.

    2. **Update `src/access/tests/BUILD.gn`**:
       - Replace `import("//build_overrides/nlunit_test.gni")` with `import("//build_overrides/pigweed.gni")`.
       - Change the target template from `chip_test_suite_using_nltest` to `chip_test_suite`.
       - Update `public_deps` to include `"${dir_pw_unit_test}"` and remove `"${chip_root}/src/lib/support:testing_nlunit"` and `"${nlunit_test_root}:nlunit-test"`.

    3. **Rewrite `src/access/tests/TestAccessControl.cpp`**:
       - Replace `#include <nlunit-test.h>` with `#include <gtest/gtest.h>`.
       - Remove `#include <lib/support/UnitTestRegistration.h>` and `CHIP_REGISTER_TEST_SUITE`.
       - Convert all test functions (e.g., `MetaTest`, `TestAclValidateAuthModeSubject`) from free functions taking `nlTestSuite*`/`void*` to `TEST_F` test cases.
       - Create a `TestAccessControl` fixture class deriving from `::testing::Test` with:
         - `SetUp()`: call `ClearAccessControl(accessControl)`.
         - `SetUpTestSuite()`: initialize the delegate, set access control, and call `Init` — move logic from original `Setup` function.
         - `TearDownTestSuite()`: call `Finish()` and `ResetAccessControlToDefault()` — move logic from original `Teardown` function.
       - Replace all `NL_TEST_ASSERT(inSuite, x)` with `EXPECT_EQ`/`EXPECT_NE`:
         - For `x == CHIP_NO_ERROR` checks, use `EXPECT_EQ(x, CHIP_NO_ERROR)`.
         - For `x != CHIP_NO_ERROR` checks, use `EXPECT_NE(x, CHIP_NO_ERROR)`.
         - For general boolean checks (e.g., `subject == kOperationalNodeId1`), use `EXPECT_EQ(subject, kOperationalNodeId1)` or `EXPECT_TRUE` where appropriate.
       - Remove the old test registration function `int TestAccessControl()` and the `nlTest` array.

    4. **Update OpenIoT SDK test component lists**:
       - Remove `accesstest` from `src/test_driver/openiotsdk/unit-tests/test_components_nl.txt`.
       - Add `accesstest` to `src/test_driver/openiotsdk/unit-tests/test_components.txt` (which lists components built against `pw_unit_test`).

    5. **Build and verify**:
       - Ensure the build succeeds with no missing symbols or undefined references.
       - Run the access control test suite to confirm all tests pass and behavior is unchanged.

573:     Target targets[kMaxTargets]   = { { 0 } };
574: 
575:     void Clear() { *this = EntryData(); }

577:     bool IsEmpty() const { return authMode == AuthMode::kNone; }
578: 
579:     size_t GetSubjectCount() const
580:     {
581:         size_t count = 0;
582:         for (auto & subject : subjects)
583:         {
584:             if (subject == kUndefinedNodeId)
585:             {
586:                 break;
587:             }
588:             count++;
589:         }
590:         return count;
591:     }

593:     void AddSubject(size_t * index, NodeId subject)
594:     {
595:         size_t count = GetSubjectCount();
596:         if (count < kMaxSubjects)
597:         {
598:             subjects[count] = subject;
599:             if (index)
600:             {
601:                 *index = count;
602:             }
603:         }
604:     }
605: 
606:     void RemoveSubject(size_t index)
607:     {
608:         size_t count = GetSubjectCount();
609:         if (index < count)
610:         {
611:             while (++index < kMaxSubjects)
612:             {
613:                 subjects[index - 1] = subjects[index];
614:             }
615:             subjects[kMaxSubjects - 1] = { 0 };
616:         }
617:     }

619:     size_t GetTargetCount() const
620:     {
621:         size_t count = 0;
622:         for (auto & target : targets)
623:         {
624:             if (target.flags == 0)
625:             {
626:                 break;
627:             }
628:             count++;
629:         }
630:         return count;
631:     }

634:     {

637:         {

641:                 *index = count;
642:             }
643:         }

660: CHIP_ERROR CompareEntry(const Entry & entry, const EntryData & entryData)
661: {
662:     AuthMode authMode = AuthMode::kNone;
663:     ReturnErrorOnFailure(entry.GetAuthMode(authMode));
664:     ReturnErrorCodeIf(authMode != entryData.authMode, CHIP_ERROR_INCORRECT_STATE);
665:     FabricIndex fabricIndex = kUndefinedFabricIndex;
666:     ReturnErrorOnFailure(entry.GetFabricIndex(fabricIndex));
667:     ReturnErrorCodeIf(fabricIndex != entryData.fabricIndex, CHIP_ERROR_INCORRECT_STATE);
668:     Privilege privilege = Privilege::kView;
669:     ReturnErrorOnFailure(entry.GetPrivilege(privilege));
670:     ReturnErrorCodeIf(privilege != entryData.privilege, CHIP_ERROR_INCORRECT_STATE);
671:     size_t subjectCount = 0;
672:     ReturnErrorOnFailure(entry.GetSubjectCount(subjectCount));
673:     ReturnErrorCodeIf(subjectCount != entryData.GetSubjectCount(), CHIP_ERROR_INCORRECT_STATE);
674:     for (size_t i = 0; i < subjectCount; ++i)
675:     {
676:         NodeId subject = kUndefinedNodeId;
677:         ReturnErrorOnFailure(entry.GetSubject(i, subject));
678:         ReturnErrorCodeIf(subject != entryData.subjects[i], CHIP_ERROR_INCORRECT_STATE);
679:     }
680:     size_t targetCount = 0;
681:     ReturnErrorOnFailure(entry.GetTargetCount(targetCount));
682:     ReturnErrorCodeIf(targetCount != entryData.GetTargetCount(), CHIP_ERROR_INCORRECT_STATE);
683:     for (size_t i = 0; i < targetCount; ++i)
684:     {
685:         Target target;
686:         ReturnErrorOnFailure(entry.GetTarget(i, target));
687:         ReturnErrorCodeIf(target != entryData.targets[i], CHIP_ERROR_INCORRECT_STATE);
688:     }
689:     return CHIP_NO_ERROR;
690: }

692: CHIP_ERROR LoadEntry(Entry & entry, const EntryData & entryData)
693: {
694:     ReturnErrorOnFailure(entry.SetAuthMode(entryData.authMode));
695:     ReturnErrorOnFailure(entry.SetFabricIndex(entryData.fabricIndex));
696:     ReturnErrorOnFailure(entry.SetPrivilege(entryData.privilege));
697:     for (size_t i = 0; i < entryData.GetSubjectCount(); ++i)
698:     {
699:         ReturnErrorOnFailure(entry.AddSubject(nullptr, entryData.subjects[i]));
700:     }
701:     for (size_t i = 0; i < entryData.GetTargetCount(); ++i)
702:     {
703:         ReturnErrorOnFailure(entry.AddTarget(nullptr, entryData.targets[i]));
704:     }
705:     return CHIP_NO_ERROR;
706: }

718: CHIP_ERROR CompareAccessControl(AccessControl & ac, const EntryData * entryData, size_t count)
719: {
720:     Entry entry;
721:     for (size_t i = 0; i < count; ++i, ++entryData)
722:     {
723:         ReturnErrorOnFailure(ac.ReadEntry(i, entry));
724:         ReturnErrorOnFailure(CompareEntry(entry, *entryData));
725:     }
726:     ReturnErrorCodeIf(ac.ReadEntry(count, entry) == CHIP_NO_ERROR, CHIP_ERROR_INCORRECT_STATE);
727:     return CHIP_NO_ERROR;
728: }

730: CHIP_ERROR LoadAccessControl(AccessControl & ac, const EntryData * entryData, size_t count)
731: {
732:     Entry entry;
733:     for (size_t i = 0; i < count; ++i, ++entryData)
734:     {
735:         ReturnErrorOnFailure(ac.PrepareEntry(entry));
736:         ReturnErrorOnFailure(LoadEntry(entry, *entryData));
737:         ReturnErrorOnFailure(ac.CreateEntry(nullptr, entry));
738:     }
739:     return CHIP_NO_ERROR;
740: }

1: # Matter Open IoT SDK unit tests
2: 
3: The unit testing approach is to create a separate application with Matter test
4: library dependence. Each Matter project component implements the set of unit
5: tests that are located in the `test` directory, e.g. `src/inet/tests`. Those
6: sources are built as a static library that can be linked to the unit test
7: application separately or as a monolithic test library. The common Matter test
8: library collects all test cases and provides the engine based on
9: [Nest Labs Unit Test](https://github.com/nestlabs/nlunit-test) to run them in
10: the application.
11: 
12: The Open IoT SDK unit tests implementation are located in the
13: `src/test_driver/openiotsdk/unit-tests` directory. This project builds a
14: separate application for each Matter component that is tested. It's built using
15: [Open IoT SDK](https://gitlab.arm.com/iot/open-iot-sdk) and run inside an
16: emulated target through the
17: [Arm FVP model for the Corstone-300 MPS3](https://developer.arm.com/downloads/-/arm-ecosystem-fvps).
18: 
19: The list of currently supported Matter's component tests:
20: 
21: ```
22: accesstest
23: AppTests
24: ASN1Tests
25: BDXTests
26: ChipCryptoTests
27: CoreTests
28: CredentialsTest
29: DataModelTests
30: InetLayerTests
31: MdnsTests
32: MessagingLayerTests
33: MinimalMdnsCoreTests
34: MinimalMdnsRecordsTests
35: MinimalMdnsRespondersTests
36: PlatformTests
37: RawTransportTests
38: RetransmitTests
39: SecureChannelTests
40: SetupPayloadTests
41: SupportTests
42: SystemLayerTests
43: TestShell
44: TransportLayerTests
45: UserDirectedCommissioningTests
46: ```
47: 
48: Each application links the specific Matter test library, executes registered
49: tests and prints the result which is the number of tests that failed.
50: 
51: ## Environment setup
52: 
53: The required environment is the same as for the Matter examples. For information
54: on how to set it up see
55: [Open IoT SDK examples environment](./openiotsdk_examples.md#environment-setup).
56: 
57: ## Configuration
58: 
59: The configuration options are the same as for the Matter examples. For
60: information on how to configure unit-tests applications see
61: [Open IoT SDK examples configuration](./openiotsdk_examples.md#configuration).
62: 
63: ## Building
64: 
65: The build process means creating a separate executable file for each Matter
66: tested component. It assumes the use of all supported test libraries and
67: creating independent applications from them.
68: 
69: You can build unit tests by using a VSCode task or by calling the build script
70: directly from the command line.
71: 
72: ### Building using the VSCode task
73: 
74: -   Open the Command Palette: <kbd>F1</kbd>
75: -   Select `Tasks: Run Task`
76: -   Select `Build Open IoT SDK unit-tests`
77: -   Decide on debug mode support
78: -   Decide on LwIP debug logs support
79: -   Choose crypto algorithm
80: -   Choose socket API
81: 
82: This will call the script with the selected parameters.
83: 
84: ### Building using CLI
85: 
86: You can call the script directly yourself.
87: 
88: ```
89: ${MATTER_ROOT}/scripts/examples/openiotsdk_example.sh unit-tests
90: ```
91: 
92: Use `--help` to get more information about the script options.
93: 
94: ## Running
95: 
96: Unit-tests applications are run independently. It runs in the background and
97: opens a telnet session. The telnet client connects to the port used by the
98: `FVP`. When the telnet process is terminated it will also terminate the `FVP`
99: instance.
100: 
101: To exit the telnet session, type <kbd>CTRL + ]</kbd>. This changes the command
102: prompt to show as:
103: 
104: ```
105: telnet>
106: ```
107: 
108: Back in the terminal, type in the word 'close' to terminate the session.
109: 
110: ```
111: telnet> close
112: ```
113: 
114: You can run specific unit test by using a VSCode task or by calling the run
115: script directly from the command line.
116: 
117: ### Running using the VSCode task
118: 
119: -   Open the Command Palette: <kbd>F1</kbd>
120: -   Select `Tasks: Run Task`
121: -   Select `Run Open IoT SDK unit-tests`

123: 
124: This will call the script with the selected example name.

132: ```
133: 
134: ## Testing
135: 
136: Run the Pytest integration test for the specific unit test application.
137: 
138: The test result can be found in the
139: `src/test_driver/openiotsdk/integration-tests/unit-tests/test_report_<unit test name>.json`
140: file.
141: 
142: You can execute the integration test for specific unit test by using a VSCode

144: 
145: ### Testing using the VSCode task
146: 
147: -   Open the Command Palette: <kbd>F1</kbd>

160: ```
161:

165: > tests:
